title: June-November low-flow dependence showed no clear change at 92 Canadian reference gauges between 1975-1999 and 2000-2024
abstract: We tested whether low June-November flow occurred in the same year more often across 92 Canadian reference gauges. We used fixed HYDAT and 2020 reference-network snapshots with complete daily records for 1975-2024. Each seasonal value is a seven-day minimum. Separate ranks in 1975-1999 and 2000-2024 fixed each gauge low-flow weight at 20%. Mean pair probability was 5.110% and 4.960%. The change was -0.150 percentage points, with a 95% three-year whole-field block range of -1.226 to +0.858. Thus, the primary test gave no clear change. Distance, drainage weighting, tail, and window checks also had ranges across zero. A fixed early threshold gave a descriptive pair-frequency rise, showing sensitivity to the event reference. Strict partial-day exclusion left one gauge; an added window check left three. These checks cannot establish flag robustness. Short periods, selected coverage, measurement flags, final archive revisions, and unmeasured climate and storage drivers limit inference. Same-year minima are not simultaneous daily droughts. The package includes code, exact source hashes, aggregate evidence, all resample scores and indices, a figure, and an arithmetic audit. External records remain outside the package.

display.caption: Low June-November flow ranks showed no clear same-year dependence change at 92 Canadian reference gauges. Left: network share with a low seasonal rank by year. Its mean is fixed at 20% in each period. Right: late-minus-early pair probability with 95% whole-field block ranges. The primary comparison is 1975-1999 against 2000-2024. Minima need not occur on the same day. The fixed sample and measurement flags limit inference.
